His film restoration company, headquartered in Burbank, California, had been credited with restoring, preserving, and, in many cases, saving early Hollywood films which may have otherwise deteriorated beyond retrieval.  Lowry developed his own techniques and technology, called the Lowry Process, which, as defined by the "Los Angeles Times" reduces "visual "noise" in motion pictures" which then makes it possible to undertake other forms of restoration, such as removing dirt and scratches, reducing flicker.  and sharpening the quality of existing images. Lowry used his process to restore and preserve more than five hundred classic films, including "Singin' in the Rain", "", "Casablanca", "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs", "Raiders of the Lost Ark", "Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom", "Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade", "Bambi", "Sunset Boulevard", and the James Bond film franchise.
